Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Vision and Tax Cuts

The Conservative manifesto centres on economic stability following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis, highlighting falling inflation, rising real wages, and returning growth. The party pledges to halve employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, saving average workers £1,350 annually. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The new "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees both State Pension and pensioners' tax-free allowance rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%.

## Family and Childcare Support

Working parents would receive 30 hours of free childcare weekly from when children are nine months old until school age, saving eligible families approximately £6,900 annually. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household system, with families retaining benefits until combined income reaches £120,000.

## Immigration and Border Security

The manifesto promises a legal cap on migration with annual parliamentary votes, continued Rwanda deportation flights, and reformed asylum rules. The party commits to stopping illegal Channel crossings and introducing stricter visa requirements, including health checks for migrants.

## Defence and National Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, representing the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The party pledges continued support for Ukraine and investment in nuclear deterrence, cyber defence, and new military technologies.

## National Service

A modernised National Service programme would become compulsory for 18-year-olds, offering either competitive military placements or community volunteering equivalent to one weekend monthly for a year.

## Housing and Infrastructure

The Conservatives target 1.6 million new homes through brownfield development, planning reforms, and abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. The £36 billion saved from HS2's second phase would fund local transport improvements, including £8.3 billion for road repairs.

## NHS and Health

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, recruiting 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Plans include expanding Pharmacy First, building 250 GP surgeries, and 50 Community Diagnostic Centres. Mental health support would expand to 100% of schools by 2030.

## Net Zero and Energy

The party maintains commitment to net zero by 2050 while promising no new green levies. Plans include annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, trebling offshore wind capacity, and building new nuclear plants including Small Modular Reactors.

## Union and Devolution

The manifesto emphasises protecting the UK's internal market and opposing Scottish independence. Direct funding would continue for Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland through extended levelling up programmes, with commitments to faithful implementation of the Windsor Framework.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Message
The Labour manifesto centres on "change" after 14 years of Conservative governance, promising to end chaos, restore economic stability, and rebuild Britain through mission-driven government focused on working people.

## Five National Missions

**1. Kickstart Economic Growth**
Labour pledges to achieve the highest sustained growth in the G7 through a new industrial strategy, a National Wealth Fund capitalised at £7.3 billion, and planning reform to build 1.5 million homes. They commit to capping corporation tax at 25%, reforming business rates, and creating a "New Deal for Working People" including banning exploitative zero-hours contracts and strengthening workers' rights.

**2. Clean Energy Superpower**
The party aims for zero-carbon electricity by 2030, establishing Great British Energy—a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland. Plans include doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind. A £6.6 billion Warm Homes Plan will upgrade five million homes. They will not issue new oil and gas exploration licences but won't revoke existing ones.

**3. Take Back Our Streets**
Labour promises to halve serious violent crime and violence against women within a decade. Key measures include recruiting thousands of neighbourhood police officers, introducing Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour, creating specialist rape units in every police force, and establishing Young Futures hubs for youth support.

**4. Break Down Barriers to Opportunity**
Education reforms include recruiting 6,500 new teachers (funded by ending private school tax exemptions), opening 3,000 primary school-based nurseries, providing free breakfast clubs in all primary schools, and reforming the curriculum. They will create Skills England and transform the apprenticeship levy into a flexible Growth and Skills Levy.

**5. NHS Fit for the Future**
Labour commits to cutting waiting times with 40,000 extra weekly appointments, doubling CT and MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and implementing a Dentistry Rescue Plan. They promise to shift toward prevention and community-based care while maintaining the NHS as publicly owned and funded.

## Strong Foundations

**National Security:** Unshakeable NATO commitment, maintaining the nuclear deterrent, conducting a Strategic Defence Review, and continuing support for Ukraine.

**Secure Borders:** Creating a Border Security Command to tackle people-smuggling gangs, scrapping the Rwanda scheme, clearing asylum backlogs, and establishing a returns enforcement unit.

**Economic Stability:** Strict fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt. No increases to income tax, National Insurance, or VAT. Abolishing non-dom tax status and closing tax loopholes.

## Constitutional Reform
Labour will remove hereditary peers from the Lords, introduce mandatory retirement at 80, give 16-17 year-olds voting rights, establish an Ethics and Integrity Commission, and reset relationships with devolved governments through a new Council of Nations and Regions.

## International Approach
The party commits to remaining outside the EU but improving trade relationships, seeking a UK-EU security pact, and restoring climate leadership through a Clean Power Alliance. They support Palestinian statehood and will restore 0.7% GNI development spending when fiscally possible.
